value.title: Derry - A literary atlas of IT
value.source_note: English EPUB supplied by the user. Publisher/edition not reliably identified in its metadata. P numbers are extraction paragraph IDs, not printed page numbers.
value.coordinates: Local fictional metric coordinates; x east, y north. No latitude/longitude or real-world georeference.

confidence.A: Text-anchored street or site relationship; coordinates still reconstructed.
confidence.B: Inferred from routes, proximity or relative position.
confidence.C: Proposed location where the book leaves a substantial gap.

constraints.text: Southwest to northeast; Barrens before downtown.
constraints.decision: Kept. The real Bangor river orientation is not transplanted.

constraints.text: Approximately 4.8 km long and 2.4 km wide.
constraints.decision: The tapered envelope measures about 4.7 km by 2.4 km along axes 35 degrees from east; boundaries are inferred, not cadastral.

constraints.text: About 3.2 km in all, with roughly 0.8 km covered.
constraints.decision: The reconstructed concrete reach is 3.37 km, the covered reach 0.80 km. Its lower end is inferred near Main Street Bridge; the final 0.63 km to the Penobscot is shown as open river. No underground network is mapped.

constraints.text: Beside Kansas/Jackson; canal to Bill's left on his descent.
constraints.decision: Kept. Jackson has an inferred bend to join the Kansas hillside crossing.

constraints.text: Kissing Bridge about 0.8 km upriver of Main Street Bridge.
constraints.decision: Kept as distinct bridges. Upper Main bends and recrosses the canal downstream.

constraints.text: Kansas/Center/Main versus Canal/Main/Kansas.
constraints.decision: One compact junction with short separate Center and Canal approaches; exact topology unresolved.

constraints.text: Library at Kansas/Costello; Costello semicircular.
constraints.decision: Kept. Community House is nearby; Market is at the other end of the loop.

constraints.text: On Kansas, about 2.4 km west of downtown, at the southern Barrens edge.
constraints.decision: Placed west-southwest, approximately 2.45 km in a straight line. This relaxes literal west to preserve the river valley and road access.

constraints.text: Later Memorial Park; northern end of army base behind West Broadway.
constraints.decision: Same park complex, separate approximate shed footprint. Earlier references to the park leave its boundary/history uncertain.

constraints.text: Same field; northeast Barrens; Old Cape to west.
constraints.decision: Single site, both historical names; approximate parcel.

constraints.text: Small western arm; split about 64 m upstream, channels meet about 180 m farther toward town.
constraints.decision: Kept locally. A fourth sheet enlarges the small branch and nearby paths.

constraints.text: Kansas bridge over tributary; path to clearing, then river.
constraints.decision: Kept as a surface access sequence; paths are approximate.

constraints.text: Truck Depot on Kansas; annex replaced by Secondhand Rose at foot of hill.
constraints.decision: Separate markers. Baseball lot behind depot, near dammed branch.

constraints.text: Route 2 northwest about 1.6 km from Witcham; school at Neibolt junction.
constraints.decision: Kept on the outer approach; yards at street end. Regional road positions remain approximate.

constraints.text: Beyond dump; by trainyards; near later Interstate overpass.
constraints.decision: Separate former coal/gravel pit. Spur and embankment shown as reconstructed.

constraints.text: Bowers at end of Kansas and on Witcham approach; Hanlon between Bowers and town.
constraints.decision: Rural road connection reconciles both descriptions. Peripheral distances are only schematic.

constraints.text: Drug store almost 4.8 km away during Eddie's attack.
constraints.decision: Used as a loose path-length check; does not determine an exact straight-line distance or every turn.

constraints.text: Some sites replaced or destroyed.
constraints.decision: A composite gazetteer retains them. It is not a simultaneous survey of one historical day.

constraints.text: The narrative mixes different accounts of waste discharge.
constraints.decision: Surface drainage runs to the valley; named facilities remain. No invented engineering model or sewer network is asserted.

constraints.text: OCR-like forms, punctuation errors and broken words occur.
constraints.decision: Original names retained when secure. Roward/Reward and several descriptive inconsistencies are recorded, not silently treated as two places.

value.method_geometry: The map prioritises neighbourhoods, routes, bridge order and water flow. It reconciles the downtown junction descriptions and places the Standpipe west-southwest of the centre. Contours, local road bends, most footprints and the vegetation pattern are illustrative. In the initial reconstruction, the canal measured approximately 3.37 km in this reconstruction, including 0.80 km under downtown; the novel gives about 3.2 km overall. A 0.63 km open reach then joined the Penobscot. That lower limit is inferred.

value.source_note: Source: Stephen King, IT (1986), supplied English EPUB. Chapter references and reconstruction decisions are in the map database. The original research notes are retained as a baseline reference.

intro.city: Four sheets form one map. Sheet 2 expands the town centre; sheets 3 and 4 reveal the Barrens and the Losers' ground. Smaller downtown sites are indexed on sheet 2.
intro.central: Both periods and the historical interludes share one plan. Old businesses and destroyed places retain their locations; dates and qualifications are in the companion notes.
intro.barrens: A tapered river valley, approximately 4.8 km long and 2.4 km wide in the novel. The border, contours, vegetation and footpaths are reconstructed.
intro.camp: The precise shape of this small area is inferred. The western branch, the path from the Kansas bridge and the separate entry cylinder preserve the book's local relationships.

local_relationships: 44  The small western arm is dammed. The broader eastern arm remains a distinct channel.
43  The clubhouse and smoke-hole are one place. Its stated width is about 1.5 m; the numbered symbol is enlarged for reading.
45  Silver is hidden under the bridge over the tributary. The route to the clearing follows the slope down to the river.
47  The entry cylinder is drawn separately from Pumphouse #3 and from Patrick's trail-end cylinder.
Paths and vegetation describe a plausible landscape. Their individual bends and boundaries are not supplied by King.

value.texture: Preserved generated woodland, marsh, buildings and minor landforms; each is editable vector geometry. They are illustrative, not surveyed.
value.terrain: Deterministic conceptual surface. No measured elevations.

feature.name: Denbrough house
feature.note: High on Witcham Street, near the hill crest. The address number, plot and orientation of the house are unspecified. Georgie's room and Bill's garage workshop are included here.

feature.name: Georgie's storm drain
feature.note: On Witcham Street, close to Jackson, downhill from the Denbrough house. The drain is upstream of the junction on this reconstruction; the exact kerb position is uncertain.

feature.name: Grace Baptist Church
feature.note: At Witcham and Jackson. Its clock and steeple figure in the final storm. The chosen corner is reconstructed.

feature.name: Derry Elementary School
feature.note: On Jackson Street, with a view toward the Witcham junction. Charter Street and Derry Park are near the playground; the building footprint is illustrative.

feature.name: Derry Park
feature.note: A public park near the elementary school. It is distinct from Bassey, McCarron and Memorial Parks. The boundary is inferred.

feature.name: Ben Hanscom home
feature.note: Ben is three blocks from home at the canal during his winter encounter. No street address is established. This is a candidate residential position within that walking range, not a recovered address.

feature.name: 127 Lower Main Street
feature.note: Beverly Marsh's childhood apartment; the Mrs Kersh encounter in 1985. The street number is explicit. Block lengths and the building plot are reconstructed.

feature.name: Richie Tozier home
feature.note: The house and porch are described, but no recoverable street address was found. This residential position is a cartographic proposal, chosen within cycling reach of Bill and the school.

feature.name: Eddie Kaspbrak home
feature.note: No defensible street address is established in the examined passages. This is a proposed position in the residential district, not an identification of a named street.

feature.name: Stan Uris home
feature.note: Domestic chores and the family home are mentioned, but these do not locate a plot. A residential position is proposed solely to make the map usable; it has the weakest location status.

feature.name: 61 Palmer Lane
feature.note: Mike Hanlon's adult home and garage, where Silver is repaired. Palmer Lane is a one-block connector between Jackson and Main. The number 61 is explicit; the plot is reconstructed.

feature.name: Derry Public Library
feature.note: At Kansas Street and one end of semicircular Costello Avenue. The adult library is in front, the children's wing behind, joined by a glass corridor. This is also Mike's workplace and the site of Henry's attack.

feature.name: Derry Community House
feature.note: About a block from the library, on the Kansas/Costello corridor. The precise frontage is inferred. Kept distinct from City Center and the Town House hotel.

feature.name: Costello Avenue Market
feature.note: Near the other junction of Costello Avenue and Kansas Street. Eddie's arm is broken outside the shop. Costello is drawn as a loop, as described.

feature.name: Aladdin Theater
feature.note: On Main Street, on the same side as Nan's and across from Freese's. Its side exit opens into a fenced alley. It is not automatically equated with the earlier Bijou.

feature.name: Nan's Luncheonette
feature.note: Beside the Aladdin, with the escape alley between them. The mapped plots express adjacency rather than measured facades.

feature.name: Freese's Department Store
feature.note: Opposite the Aladdin/Nan's side of Main Street. Richie evades Henry in its toy department. The department arrangement is not mapped.

feature.name: Center Street Drug Store
feature.note: Mr Keene's shop on Center Street, backing onto Richard's Alley. Chapter 10 says it has gone; later passages still name it. Shown as a historical footprint, without inventing a replacement business.

feature.name: Richard's Alley / mini-mall
feature.note: A pedestrian connector between Main and Center, behind the drug store. Penny-pitching site; later converted into a mini-mall.

feature.name: Derry Town House
feature.note: Hotel on Upper Main Street. Bassey Park is about 0.8 km farther up and across the street. The hotel is separate from the civic buildings.

feature.name: Jade of the Orient
feature.note: On the Pasture Road / Mall Road corridor, beyond the mall when travelling out from downtown. The restaurant grounds are proposed.

feature.name: Kitchener Ironworks / Derry Mall
feature.note: The mall occupies the former Ironworks field at the northeastern end of the Barrens. Old Cape lies behind it to the west. Mike's giant-bird encounter occurs among the ruins. The ruins and mall share one site marker.

feature.name: City Center & Paul Bunyan
feature.note: The statue faces Outer Canal Street from the City Center lawn, near Bassey Park. The text gives almost 1.6 km from Freese's to City Center. The straight separation here is about 1.6 km; the precise walking route remains unresolved.

feature.name: Bassey Park & fairgrounds
feature.note: Northeast of downtown, beside the canal, facing Derry High School across it. Includes the carnival and later horse-racing grounds; their precise internal layout is conjectural.

feature.name: Kissing Bridge
feature.note: Covered footbridge joining Bassey Park and Derry High School. It is about 0.8 km upriver from Main Street Bridge. It is not the bridge from which Adrian Mellon is thrown.

feature.name: Derry High School
feature.note: Across the canal from Bassey Park, connected by the Kissing Bridge. Building and playing-field outlines are inferred.

feature.name: Main Street Bridge / Adrian Mellon
feature.note: Adrian Mellon is thrown from this road bridge. It is downstream of the Kissing Bridge, near the Falcon and bus station. Main Street is bent to cross the canal again beyond the park; that road geometry is an inference.

feature.name: The Falcon
feature.note: Beside the bus terminal, within a short walk of Main Street Bridge. The pair pass the terminal and turn left toward the bridge. The block position is inferred.

feature.name: Bus terminal
feature.note: Adjacent to the Falcon; bright station windows are visible during the attack on Adrian. The access road and footprint are reconstructed.

feature.name: Derry Home Hospital
feature.note: The Penobscot runs behind the hospital. In 1985 the original building survives inside a much larger complex. A riverside site is plausible; no exact address is fixed.

feature.name: Secondhand Rose, Secondhand Clothes
feature.note: At the bottom of Up-Mile Hill, occupying the former Tracker Brothers' Annex. Bill finds Silver here. This is a different location from the Truck Depot and its ballfield.

feature.name: Derry Theological Seminary
feature.note: On Kansas Street behind Warehouse Row. Beverly escapes through a gap beside the Tracker annex, crosses a fence and uses the seminary grounds. The plot is arranged to make this route possible.

feature.name: Derry Standpipe
feature.note: On Kansas Street at Memorial Park, roughly 2.4 km west of downtown and near the Barrens' southern edge. This plan interprets west broadly as west-southwest; no surveyed elevation is claimed. The Johnson boy is found almost at its foot in December 1984 (First Interlude, P1425).

feature.name: Memorial Park
feature.note: Standpipe park, with a sundial and birdbath. The Black Spot is placed in a former portion of the park; the present boundary is reconstructed. Stan's birdwatching is included here.

feature.name: The Black Spot - former site
feature.note: The Second Interlude explicitly places the club where Memorial Park later stands, at the northern end of the old army base behind West Broadway. Exact shed position is unknown.

feature.name: Derry Army Base - former grounds
feature.note: The base extends south from behind West Broadway. Ridgeline Road branches from Witcham Road at its entrance. Its outline is a compact proposal; the novel describes more than 0.4 km2.

feature.name: Mount Hope Cemetery
feature.note: Georgie's burial place is named. The novel passages used do not determine its position within Derry. This edge-of-town placement is deliberately approximate and does not copy Bangor coordinates.

feature.name: 29 Neibolt Street
feature.note: Abandoned house near the end of Neibolt Street, just outside the trainyards. The text calls it a former red Cape Cod. Its plot and nearby houses are reconstructed from the approach route. Lisa Albrecht is found directly across the street in October 1984 (First Interlude, P1425).

feature.name: Neibolt Street Church School
feature.note: Mike's school, at Route 2 and Neibolt Street. Route 2 runs northwest for about 1.6 km from its Witcham junction. Neibolt continues toward the yards.

feature.name: Derry trainyards / former station
feature.note: Neibolt ends at the yard parking area. The yards adjoin the Barrens near the old coal/gravel pit. Six converging tracks are mentioned; the sidings shown are illustrative.

feature.name: Tracker Brothers' Truck Depot
feature.note: On Kansas Street, behind Kossuth on Eddie's walk toward downtown. The back lot slopes toward the Barrens. Kept separate from the downtown Tracker annex.

feature.name: Tracker ballfield
feature.note: Immediately behind the depot. A home run ends near the stream later dammed by the Losers. The field and fence are illustrative; its proximity to the dam is preserved.

feature.name: Losers' clearing & clubhouse
feature.note: Accessible by the path from the Kansas Street bridge and near the river. The smoke-hole is the clubhouse itself, not a second location. The exact clearing position is inferred. Only its surface entrance is mapped.

feature.name: The Losers' dam
feature.note: On the smaller western arm, not across the entire broad Kenduskeag. The split is about 64 m upstream and the reunion of the channels roughly 180 m farther toward town. The detailed sheet follows that local arrangement.

feature.name: Kansas Street wooden bridge
feature.note: Bridge over a small drainage tributary, not a bridge over the main Kenduskeag. Bill hides Silver beneath it. It is the familiar access point used again by the adults.

feature.name: Ben's fall into the Barrens
feature.note: Through the whitewashed Kansas Street railing above a steep slope and culvert. His subsequent flight toward Old Cape puts this on the Kansas bank; the exact break in the fence is unknown.

feature.name: Entry pumping cylinder
feature.note: The broken pumping cylinder used to enter the drains, beside the Kenduskeag, downstream of the lightning-struck tree. It is not explicitly identified as municipal Pumphouse #3. Only the surface access is shown.

feature.name: City Dump / waste-treatment site
feature.note: In a gravel pit, reached by Old Lyme Street from Kansas Street. In 1985 the dump has been replaced by a modern waste-treatment plant. Their exact footprints are proposed.

feature.name: Patrick's refrigerator
feature.note: A discarded Amana refrigerator beside a spruce on the Kansas-side approach to the dump. Patrick's trail leads away from the junk cars toward a pumping cylinder by the river; it is not assigned to the later entry cylinder.

feature.name: Apocalyptic Rockfight / old coal pit
feature.note: Abandoned coal/gravel pit beyond the dump, beside the trainyards and near the later Interstate overpass. This is a separate pit from the active city dump.

feature.name: Derry Pumphouse #3
feature.note: A municipal sewage-pumping facility in the Barrens. Its exact site is not given. This candidate downstream position preserves separation from the small access cylinders along the banks.

feature.name: Blood-oath riverbank
feature.note: The children emerge from a pumping cylinder, gather at the river and later climb to Kansas Street. Exact identity of the exit and the oath bank is not fixed. The marker represents a plausible nearby stretch.

feature.name: Ben's winter canal encounter
feature.note: At an open canal reach from which Ben looks southwest for about 0.8 km toward the Barrens. A street-side position just before the covered reach is proposed.

feature.name: Eddie Corcoran / canal bank
feature.note: At Bassey Park beside the canal. The boy's last movements constrain the park and bank, but not a precise tree or coordinate.

feature.name: Bradley Gang massacre
feature.note: At the Main/Canal/Kansas junction near Machen's and the courthouse. Chapter 5 calls the approaches Kansas/Center/Main. The plan treats these as one compact junction complex, not two separate massacres.

feature.name: Machen's Sporting Goods
feature.note: At the massacre intersection within firing distance of the courthouse and theater marquee. The precise side of the junction is inferred.

feature.name: Courthouse & jail
feature.note: Steps and clock overlook the central intersection. The jail is treated as part of the civic complex. Building dimensions and the relationship to the separately named Town Hall are not established.

feature.name: War Memorial / canal portal
feature.note: At the point where the canal goes underground. The monument plot is reconstructed. It is distinct from Memorial Park by the Standpipe.

feature.name: Silver Dollar - historical vicinity
feature.note: A canal-area beerjoint with an escape to Exchange Street from its rear privy. The street block and exact building position are not securely given. The same passage also calls it the Sleepy Silver Dollar.

feature.name: Claude Heroux lynching - vicinity
feature.note: An elm overhanging the canal on Canal Street, reached from the jail. The individual tree and its coordinate are unknown.

feature.name: Derrie settlement / burned house
feature.note: One burned house stood approximately at the later Witcham/Jackson intersection. This marker locates that house vicinity, not the full boundary of the vanished settlement.

feature.name: Clements home / disappearance
feature.note: At Kansas Street and Kossuth Lane. Kossuth descends about 400 m and ends abruptly at the Barrens. This junction is kept separate from the Kaspbrak home, which Eddie says was not here.

feature.name: Betty Ripsom discovery - vicinity
feature.note: At the turnpike construction area on Outer Jackson Street. The exact construction parcel is unknown.

feature.name: Torrault Stream / Cheryl Lamonica
feature.note: Cheryl's remains are found in Torrault Stream. Its discharge is associated with the Penobscot. The tributary corridor shown is a hydrologically plausible proposal.

feature.name: McCarron Park
feature.note: Between the school neighbourhood and the Costello/library walk. Contains a sledding hill. Shape and detailed location are inferred from the walking route.

feature.name: Bowers farm - approximate
feature.note: Near the Newport line; described both at the end of Kansas Street and on the Witcham Road approach. The roads are joined in the rural fringe to reconcile the descriptions. No literal regional location is claimed.

feature.name: Hanlon farm - approximate
feature.note: On the same rural approach as the Bowers place, with land reaching toward the Kenduskeag. Its road distance to the Ironworks is described as a little over 6.4 km. The fringe placement is approximate.

feature.name: Kleen-Kloze Washateria
feature.note: At Main and Cony, two blocks from a view of the canal. The children wash the bloody rags here. The shown building is a retained former site.

feature.name: 73 Charter Street
feature.note: Home of Eddie and Dorsey Corcoran and the Macklins. Charter is near the elementary playground; the address is explicit, the position along the street inferred.

feature.name: Koala Inn & Holiday Inn
feature.note: Adjacent motels on Outer Jackson Street, separated by a raised walkway. Tom and Audra stay here. The location along Outer Jackson is approximate.

feature.name: Kitchener Precision Tool & Die
feature.note: Bill and Richie obtain molds for the silver balls here. No street address is given. An industrial-fringe position is proposed, separate from the destroyed Ironworks.

feature.name: Bijou - historical vicinity
feature.note: A theater marquee provides a firing position in the Bradley Gang episode. Its relationship to the later Aladdin is not stated; the two are not merged.

feature.name: Eastern Star - former hotel
feature.note: At the end of Exchange Street. Demolished during urban renewal before the adults return. The street end is proposed.

feature.name: Traveller's Rest - former hotel
feature.note: On Torrault Street, removed during urban renewal. The relation of that street to the similarly named stream is a reconstruction.

feature.name: Derry Heights / old country club
feature.note: Heights seen across the Barrens, beyond Old Cape, with an earlier country club. The hill shape and club position are proposed.

feature.name: Old Cape
feature.note: Low-income district on the western bank of the Barrens, west of the Ironworks/mall. Exact street pattern and buildings are reconstructed.

feature.name: Sherburn Woods
feature.note: A more fashionable development beyond Old Cape. Only that relationship is supplied; extent and geometry are proposed.

feature.name: West Broadway houses
feature.note: The Mueller, Bowie and Tracker houses occupy the prestigious West Broadway blocks. The Mueller house is near Witcham and the Bowie house four houses away. The cluster is placed north of the old base; individual plots are illustrative.

feature.name: Slingshot practice / junk cars
feature.note: On the Kansas-side approach to the dump, among junked cars below the pit's steep side. Beverly practices with the Bullseye here. Car positions and the firing area are illustrative.

feature.name: Patrick's trail-end cylinder
feature.note: At the river after the blood trail from the dump and refrigerator. The text does not equate it with Pumphouse #3 or the later entry cylinder; the reconstruction keeps them distinct.

feature.name: Rhulin Farms - approach only
feature.note: Named on the Route 7 / Witcham Road approach, before the Bowers and Hanlon places when entering town. Symbol placed near the sheet edge; distances on this peripheral approach are schematic.

feature.name: Merit Street culvert
feature.note: The culvert discovery associated with Matthew Clements, at a blocked-off part of Merit Street near the turnpike works. Merit is in Old Cape. Exact position of the culvert is proposed.

feature.name: Upper Kenduskeag logging camp
feature.note: Nine wintering loggers were found murdered at a camp on the Upper Kenduskeag, at a tip of the Barrens. Upper suggests an upstream end, but the word tip is ambiguous. This southwest riverside site is a proposal; neither the cabin nor its exact bank can be recovered.

feature.name: John Markson house
feature.note: Site of the poisoning of the Markson family. No address or relationship to a named street is supplied; no pin is assigned.

feature.name: Ninth Street Middle School
feature.note: Named in Mike's brief biography. No usable street relationship was recovered. That biography also names Derry Elementary, while the childhood scenes place him at the Neibolt Street Church School; the inconsistency is retained.

feature.name: Derry Town Hall
feature.note: The whistle on Town Hall ends Ben's winter trance. Its location and relationship to the courthouse or City Center are not established; these buildings are not silently merged.

feature.name: Juniper Hill
feature.note: Psychiatric institution outside Derry, in the Augusta area. Included as an off-map narrative location, not moved into the town plan.

feature.name: Cycle Shoppe
feature.note: Bill buys Silver here before its later rediscovery at Secondhand Rose. The original bicycle shop is a distinct business; its street position is not established.

feature.name: Veronica Grogan storm drain
feature.note: A drain where Veronica is found. No secure street address was recovered. It is not equated with Georgie's drain.

feature.name: Hockstetter family home
feature.note: Site of Avery's death and Patrick's domestic history. The Engstrom home stands one block over and behind it, but no usable town position is given.

feature.name: Bradley Gang rented farmhouse
feature.note: Just over the Newport line, near the later Rhulin Farms. This rural hiding place is outside the detailed reconstruction; no separate coordinate is assigned.

feature.name: Dennis Torrio discovery area
feature.note: In the Barrens. Georgie's photograph is found by a fallen log within about 3 m of the body. This is a significant clue before Mike calls the others, but the text does not locate the log within the valley.

source.title: Stephen King - IT: Inspiration
source.role: Author's explanation: Bangor's canal and a childhood library in Stratford informed the novel. Used to establish multiple real inspirations, not street coordinates.

source.title: Stephen King - Fair Extension: Inspiration
source.role: Author's general statement connecting Derry and Bangor. No places from the other story were added.

source.title: City of Bangor - Stormwater
source.role: Primary background for urban runoff and tributaries. Used only to check the plausibility of the reconstructed surface landscape.

source.title: City of Bangor - Kenduskeag Stream Parkway map
source.role: Official real-world map inspected as an urban river-corridor analogue. Its modern street geometry, scale and landmarks were not transferred to Derry.

source.title: Bangor Water District - Thomas Hill Standpipe
source.role: Primary architectural analogue. The real tank differs from the novel's stated dimensions and history; book details have priority.

source.title: Bangor Public Library - Augustus Koch, Bangor 1875
source.role: Historical cartographic context and catalog record. Not used as a measured base map.

source.title: Alissa Burger - Mapping Derry (15 December 2023)
source.role: Source audit: describes maps mixing novel, screen adaptations and other novels. Those maps were excluded as geographic authority.
